handbook/annex/p15/radon-nikodym.tex has no \section heading, so its 13 proofs are typeset under the preceding annex section "Countable products and real codings: proofs" (handbook/annex/p15/countable-product-measures.tex line 2). Coverage is unaffected; navigation to these proofs is misleading.

The general Cantor plateau computation uses, without stating it, that stage intervals are ordered left to right in binary order of their words (bit 0 = left third, bit 1 = right third, nested). This follows directly from the displayed successor intervals at 533-540 and was not treated as a missing step; one sentence would make it explicit.

The semialgebra definition requires the empty set to be a member; Durrett's definition (held PDF p.11, printed p.3) states only intersection closure and the complement property, although his Example 1.1.5 includes the empty set and Theorem 1.1.9 presupposes mu(empty)=0. The tightening is harmless but is not flagged as a variant, unlike the premeasure terminology at body 48-50.

"The other order similarly gives G(z-x)" (line 117) stands for the mirror of the displayed computation at 113-115, i.e. nu((-inf,z-x])=G(z-x) by definition of G; the result is stated and Tonelli equality is argued, so the second cumulative identity of C005 was judged written. Other hedge words in the four annexes (measurable-probability 139, 405, 454; radon-nikodym 36, 57, 173; measure-extension 296) each precede or accompany the written step.

Section 157.5 is titled "... and mixed distributions", but none of the 76 owed components treats the decomposition of a real law into atomic, absolutely continuous and continuous singular parts. That material is on route in sec:p15-w02b-p15-002-mixed-laws (toc line 1 lists 157.5, 157.6, 157.7). It is outside the owed components and the empty duty list of this assessment and was not assessed here.
